extraction.name: Self-Contradictory Instructions (SCI)
extraction.description: A multimodal benchmark for evaluating large multimodal models on recognizing self-contradictory instructions across language-language and vision-language paradigms. It contains 20,000 conflicts and includes eight tasks. The dataset is constructed using an automatic dataset creation framework called AutoCreate.
extraction.creator: Jin Gao, Lei Gan, Yuankai Li, Yixin Ye, and Dequan Wang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was constructed using a novel automatic dataset creation framework, AutoCreate, which uses programs and large language models in a cyclic generator-decorator-cleaner process. Human experts and LLMs double-checked quality, and human experts manually selected the SCI-Base and SCI-Core subsets.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Task-relevant seed data, generated language and vision data, and for SemanticConflict, external data from ImageNet.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For language-language conflicts, contradictory instructions were created by pairing rules with violations, attributes with opposite descriptions, exclusive instructions, or forbidden words with questions requiring the forbidden word. For vision-language conflicts, images or captions were modified to introduce conflicts, including OCR text images, altered charts, geometric shapes with mismatched descriptions, and substituted labels for ImageNet-based semantic conflicts.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A cleaner removed data that did not meet quality standards, and human experts rigorously checked the generated dataset. The dataset was also manually split into SCI-Core and SCI-Base subsets.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human experts and LLMs double-checked the quality of generated data. The paper does not describe a separate human labeling protocol for annotations beyond conflict generation and quality checking.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For evaluation, replies were judged by human experts and by LLM evaluators such as GPT-4 and ChatGLM. The paper reports agreement statistics between evaluators, including Spearman correlation and concordance rate.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Large language models were used in AutoCreate for generation and quality checking; GPT-4 and ChatGLM were used as evaluation agents.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper states that the benchmark, AutoCreate framework, and CaP approach have social implications by providing a standardized platform to assess and improve LMMs' handling of conflicting instructions, advancing human-computer interaction, promoting inclusivity in AI research, and fostering trust and reliability in AI systems.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark only includes language-language and vision-language paradigms. More modalities may be added later. No fine-grained control is introduced to determine conflict degree, and the paper does not provide a detailed study of attention mechanisms under conflict instructions.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation/benchmarking of large multimodal models on instruction conflict detection; the paper also uses the benchmark for testing prompting methods such as zero-shot, chain-of-thought, self-consistency, few-shot, and Cognitive Awakening Prompting.
